items.title: Dynamic Web Extended User Guide
items.text:
Welcome to the online User Guide for Dynamic Web Extended (DWE), an addon for the Gramps genealogy application.

Dynamic Web Extended builds on the standard Dynamic Web Report (DWR), providing additional features for presenting and exploring family history on a website.

items.title: About this guide
items.text:
This guide is intended for:

  • Website creators, who install DWE, configure its options and generate a family history website.
  • Website visitors, who use the generated website to explore people, families, events and other information.

The guide covers installation, website creation, the main features of DWE, configuration options and technical information.

items.title: 1 Introduction
items.text:
This is a guide for

  • Website visitors, describing what they will see and how they can use the Dynamic Web Extended website.

  • Website report creators, explaining how to use the Dynamic Web Extended addon to generate website pages from a Gramps family tree.

Tested in Gramps 5.2 and 6.0

Revised November 2026, John Vitlin

items.title: 1.1 Summary
items.text:
Dynamic Web Extended (called DWE for short) is a Gramps report addon for creating interactive genealogy websites. It is derived from the Gramps Dynamic Web Report (DWR for short), originally developed by Pierre Bélissent and others, and retains the main features and layout of that report while adding several extensions.

DWE is intended for family-history websites and is useful to explore not only the details recorded for an individual, but also that person's place within their wider family.

The principal additions are:

  • major new features

  • individual and family enhancements

  • website customisation

  • documentation.

DWE does not replace the standard Dynamic Web Report. It is a separate addon, so both reports can be installed and used in Gramps.

This guide concentrates on the features added or changed by DWE. For the underlying features inherited unchanged from Dynamic Web Report, the standard Gramps Dynamic Web Report documentation remains applicable. That documentation is online on the Gramps website.

items.title: 1.2 About this guide
items.text:
Features inherited unchanged from the standard Gramps Dynamic Web Report are not described in detail.

DWE has been tested with Gramps 5.2 and Gramps 6.0. The test operating system was Windows 10. The screenshots in this guide may differ slightly between Gramps versions, but the operation of DWE is the same. Many screenshots use the Mainz website template, but now there are other themes available some screenshots use those themes.

The web pages of the report can be displayed in different formats at any time, determined by a visitor via a Configuration option. The configuration button (shown as a gear icon) is at the top right of the report’s title bar. The Use tabbed panels instead of sections option determines whether the pages are displayed in tabbed panels or as linear sections. The screenshots in the guide assume the website user has selected the tabbed panels view, but the information in this guide applies to all views.

items.title: 1.3 Report and website terminology
items.text:
Gramps uses the term report for the Dynamic Web Report. Dynamic Web Extended is similar and is selected from the Gramps Reports menu. Running the report generates a set of web pages that are viewed in a web browser.

In this guide, DWE report generally refers to the report being created in Gramps, while DWE website refers to the generated result viewed in a browser. They are two ways of referring to the same generated family-history material.

items.title: 2 Main features
items.text: DWE adds these capabilities to the standard Dynamic Web Report:

items.title: 2.1 Major features
items.text:
• Extended Events — combines a person's own events with relevant events from parents, siblings, spouses and children to provide a chronological view of the family around them.

  • Lifespans — a graphical display showing how the lives of a person and their immediate family overlap.

  • Tree Viewer — an interactive graphical family-tree display using a bundled version of the Topola Genealogy Viewer.

  • Citations — provides a searchable and sortable table of citations associated with an individual, including links to the information being cited. Visitors can choose between the table and the original list.

  • Statistics — provides summaries of genealogical information, including people, families and events.

  • Notable Records — highlights interesting genealogical records involving ages, marriages, children and families, with a visitor-selectable number of results.

  • Calendar — displays birthdays, marriage anniversaries and death anniversaries throughout the year, with configurable event types, date ranges and options for displaying living people.

items.title: 2.2 Individual and family enhancements
items.text:
• Event participants — improved handling of witnesses, clergy and other participants, including their roles.

  • Tracking — shows how people in the website are related to one or more selected people.

  • Why Me — allows the website creator to explain why a particular person has been included in the family tree.

  • Story — provides a short introduction or summary near the top of a person's page.

  • Multiple-family clarity — changes parts of the family display, making multiple families and less usual family structures easier to understand.

  • Expandable individual details — provides a collapsible heading on individual pages, allowing visitors to switch between a compact summary showing the person's name and lifespan and the full individual details.

items.title: 2.3 Website customisation and documentation
items.text:
• Markdown notes — allows selected Gramps notes written in Markdown to be rendered as formatted content.

  • Local Labels — allows selected labels in the generated website to be customised without modifying the program code.

  • Website themes — the original Default and Mainz styles, plus five new Bootswatch themes: Cerulean, Flatly, Journal, Readable and United.

  • Theme selection — visitors can change the website's appearance using the available styles.

  • Quick Guide — provides a guide within the generated website, with an editable Markdown source that allows the website creator to customise instructions for visitors.

  • Documentation – including user guides to new features and changes, and short readme documents.

DWE also includes many smaller enhancements to relationships, events, place names, indexes and other items in the generated website.

items.title: 3 History
items.text:
Dynamic Web Extended began as a personal modification of the Gramps Dynamic Web Report (DWR), originally developed by Pierre Bélissent and others. The word ‘Dynamic’ can indicate that the website is configurable - site visitors can change the look by using Configuration options. ‘Dynamic’ also indicates that each page is prepared dynamically in the browser from data files as required; the pages are not individual static pages.

The first version was called Dynamic Web Report B (DWR B). It began with changes to the Events display and gradually acquired additional features intended to make it easier to understand people in the context of their families.

Development continued from time to time. The family timeline developed into the current Lifespans visualisation, Markdown note support was added, and the Topola Viewer was integrated and bundled with the addon to provide the Tree Viewer. Other changes improved events, relationships, historical place names, translations and local viewing.

Because the addon became substantially more than a modified copy of Dynamic Web Report, it was reorganised and renamed Dynamic Web Extended (DWE). The new name reflects its purpose: retaining the foundation and much of the functionality of Dynamic Web Report while extending it with additional ways of presenting and exploring family-history information.

items.title: 4 Installing Dynamic Web Extended
items.text:
Dynamic Web Extended is distributed as a Gramps addon. It uses the standard Gramps addon distribution and installation mechanism and can be installed and updated through the Gramps Addon Manager.

DWE is installed separately from the standard Dynamic Web Report. Installing DWE does not replace or modify the DWR, and both can be available in Gramps at the same time.

DWE has been tested with Gramps 5.2 and Gramps 6.0. The addon supplied for each version of Gramps is built specifically for that Gramps version.

items.title: 4.1 Installing the addon
items.text:
Dynamic Web Extended can be installed using the Gramps Addon Manager. DWE is distributed through an addon project containing versions of the addon appropriate for supported versions of Gramps.

To install:

1. Open Gramps and select Edit → Addon Manager or click the Addon Manager icon.

2. Create a new addon project (you could name it DWE) using the URL appropriate to your Gramps version:

For Gramps 5.2

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/johnvitlin/DWE-Addons/main/gramps52

For Gramps 6.0

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/johnvitlin/DWE-Addons/main/gramps60

Figure 1- creating an Addon project

3. Refresh for available addons.

4. Once the project has been enabled, Dynamic Web Extended will appear in the list of available addons. You can find it by entering ‘dynamic’ in the search bar.

Figure 2- selecting the report

Select and install it. If an earlier version of DWE is already installed, the Addon Manager will instead indicate that an update is available and provide an Update button.

5. Restart Gramps if prompted.

Once installed, the report is available in the Gramps menus under Reports → Web Pages → Dynamic Web Extended.

The distribution files and user documentation are maintained at:

https://github.com/johnvitlin/DWE-Addons

items.title: 4.2 Upgrading DWE
items.text:
When installing a newer version of Dynamic Web Extended, use the addon manager. Your genealogy data is not stored in the DWE addon directory, so upgrading the addon does not alter your family tree.

If you have manually modified files within your DWE installation, make a copy of those changes before upgrading, as addon files may be replaced during installation.

items.title: 4.3 Removing DWE
items.text: DWE can be removed without affecting the standard Dynamic Web Report or your Gramps family-tree data. Previously generated DWE websites are also independent of the installed addon and can continue to be viewed.

items.title: 5 Creating a Dynamic Web Extended website
items.text: Once installed in Gramps Dynamic Web Extended is run in the same way as the standard Gramps Dynamic Web Report.
path: 5 Creating a Dynamic Web Extended website

items.title: 5.1 Selecting the DWE report
items.text:
In Gramps, open the family tree for which you want to create the website. Select Reports → Web Pages → Dynamic Web Extended from the Gramps menu.

Figure 3- DWE report location

You will see the report’s options pages.

Figure 4- DWE options display
path: 5 Creating a Dynamic Web Extended website

items.title: 5.2 Choosing where to create the website
items.text:
Choose the Destination directory in which DWE will create the website.

DWE generates a collection of HTML, JavaScript, data and other supporting files in the directory. These files together form the website. The generated directory and its subdirectories should always be kept together.

If you generate the report again into the same location, the website files are regenerated from the current Gramps data and the current options you have selected.
path: 5 Creating a Dynamic Web Extended website

items.title: 5.3 Selecting the people to include
items.text: As with the Dynamic Web Report, you can use a Gramps filter to determine which people are included in the generated website. The selected people, together with the other report options, determine the information that DWE exports for your family tree.
path: 5 Creating a Dynamic Web Extended website

items.title: 5.4 DWE-specific options
items.text:
Many report options are inherited from the Dynamic Web Report and behave in the same way. DWE adds options for its additional features, on the DWE Options page.

Additional options control features such as Events, Lifespans, Tree Viewer, Tracking, Why Me, Story, Markdown notes and Local Labels. This guide explains how each option affects a feature.

The DWE-specific options for a website creator are described together in Chapter 21, DWE Options The changes to the website display from selecting those options are explained in the rest of this guide.
path: 5 Creating a Dynamic Web Extended website

items.title: 5.5 Generating the report
items.text:
After selecting the required options, click OK to generate the report. Depending on the size of the family tree and the options selected, generation may take some time.

The resulting website can be copied to a web server for publication, or it can be viewed locally on a computer. Local viewing is described below.

Browser compatibility: Dynamic Web Extended is intended for modern web browsers, such as Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Opera and Safari. Microsoft Internet Explorer is not supported.
path: 5 Creating a Dynamic Web Extended website

items.title: 5.6 Regenerating an existing report
items.text:
A DWE report can be generated again into an existing destination directory. Files generated by DWE are updated as required. Files that have not changed may be left untouched, as with the original Dynamic Web Report.

Files that you have added to the destination directory yourself are not automatically removed. This also means that files created by an earlier version or configuration of DWE may remain after they are no longer required. For this reason, when preparing a clean copy of a website for publication, it is advisable to generate the report into a new or empty directory.
path: 5 Creating a Dynamic Web Extended website

items.title: 5.7 Deploying the website
items.text: The website folders and files are generated by DWE into a folder on your computer. To use the website on a web server, transfer that folder and its contents to your web server.
path: 5 Creating a Dynamic Web Extended website

items.title: 5.8 Local viewing
items.text:
A DWE website can be viewed locally on your computer or another computer. To use it on another computer, copy the whole directory in which the report was created (you selected the directory when you created the report).

To use all DWE features when viewing the report locally, it should be opened through a local web server. You don’t need to create one yourself, DWE created a file to make that easy on Windows.
path: 5 Creating a Dynamic Web Extended website

items.title: 5.8.1 Start the website
items.text:
Open the report directory and double-click View report locally.bat, or right-click it and select Open.

Figure 5- example batch file folder location

A small Windows command window opens and starts a local web server on your computer. The DWE home page then opens automatically in your browser. Leave the command window open while you are viewing the website.

Figure 6 - Windows command window and DWE report opened in the browser

When you have finished, close the DWE browser page and then close the command window.
path: 5 Creating a Dynamic Web Extended website

items.title: 5.8.2 How it works
items.text:
Using View report locally.bat starts a built-in web server and allows the Tree Viewer to open. It also allows OpenStreetMap maps to work.

OpenStreetMap requires map requests from websites to include information identifying the referring website. Opening the report through a local web server allows the browser to provide this information.

Note: The local web server runs only on your computer, and report data is not uploaded to the internet. Features that obtain information from external services, such as OpenStreetMap map tiles, still require an internet connection.
path: 5 Creating a Dynamic Web Extended website

items.title: 6 Person pages
items.text: Most of the changes in DWE can be seen in the individual’s Person pages. Main features added to the page such as extended events, lifespans display and so on are described in their own chapters later in this guide.

items.title: 6.1 Expandable individual details
items.text:
In DWE the information at the top of an individual’s page can be expanded or collapsed. By default, the details are collapsed, providing a more compact layout.

This feature stabilises the top of the page when navigating between individuals, particularly when some have more biographical information than others.

Figure 7- collapsed person details

The heading displays the individual’s short name, gender and lifespan. The short name uses the format selected by the report creator in the Report page of the report’s Options.

Click on the heading to expand the details:

Figure 8- expanded person details

Expanded, it displays the full individual details, including additional names, biographical information and other information available for that person. Click it again to collapse the section.

DWE remembers whether the section was expanded or collapsed when you move between individuals, so you do not need to adjust it each time you open another person's page. The expandable individual-details header works independently of the tabbed-panel setting in Configuration.

items.title: 7 Events
items.text:
DWE substantially extends the Events display provided by the original Dynamic Web Report. The Events tab now combines a person’s own events with important events in the lives of close family members, creating a chronological view of the person in their family context.

For example, it can show when a person’s children were born, whether their parents were still alive at a particular time, or how events in the lives of siblings and spouses relate to the person's own events.

The Events table is a timeline display – earliest events are at the top, and later events fall below them, in date order:

Figure 9 - Events table example

The table is like the timeline displays used by many online family-tree sites. The table lists the following events for a person:

  • their individual events as usual, such as birth, residence, occupation, census, news, military service...

  • birth and death events for their direct family:

    • their children

    • their spouses

    • their siblings

    • their parents

  • Events in which the person has a role (called Participation events)

The events are combined into a single chronological display. Events without a date are placed at the beginning of the table.

items.title: 7.1 Filtering the Events display
items.text:
Checkboxes above the Events table allow visitors to control the amount of information displayed. Events can be filtered onscreen without regenerating the website.

Figure 10- Event display filters

The browser remembers the checkbox selections when navigating between person pages and when the pages are reloaded, subject to the browser's local storage settings.

items.title: 7.2 Filter events for family
items.text:
Events for Children, Spouses, Siblings and Parents can be shown or hidden independently. This helps to see events in the person's life in the context of changes within their family.

Filtering can be useful for people with large families, where displaying every birth and death may otherwise make the timeline quite long.

  • Children – show or hide birth and death events for the person’s children.

  • Spouses – show or hide birth and death events for the person’s spouse or spouses.

  • Siblings – show or hide birth and death events for brothers and sisters.

    • where two people share both birth parents, they are shown as brother, sister or sibling

    • where they share one birth parent, they are shown as half-brother, half-sister or half-sibling

    • If they do not share a birth parent, DWE shows them as non-birth brother, non-birth sister or non-birth sibling

    • The Parents & siblings tab shows the recorded parent-child relationships in more detail

  • Parents – show or hide birth and death events for the person’s parents.

items.title: 7.3 Limit events to lifespan
items.text:
The Limit events to lifespan option will restrict the events display to dated events that occurred during the person's lifetime.

  • With this filter off, the table will include events before the person was born such as a parent's birth or events involving family members after the person's death.

  • Events without a date are not included when the display is limited to the person's lifespan (because it is not known if they occurred within the lifespan).

items.title: 7.4 Filter other information
items.text:
Under Show: there are three independent controls:

  • Notes — shows or hides event notes and associated descriptive details.

  • Participants — shows or hides the other participants details.

  • Participation events — shows or hides entire event rows representing participation in another person's event.

These selections allow a visitor to switch between a detailed display and a shorter chronological list. Turning off Participants hides the participant details but retains the events themselves. Turning off Participation events removes those events from the table.

items.title: 7.5 Participants
items.text:
In Gramps, several people can be associated with the same event, each with a particular role. These roles may include Primary, Witness, Clergy, Celebrant, or a user-defined role. The additional participants and their roles are displayed in the Details column.

Gramps has a default set of roles, and new roles can be assigned by the Gramps database creator. This feature is described in the Gramps wiki.

items.title: 7.6.1 Who
items.text:
The Who column identifies the principal people associated with an event, excluding the person whose page is shown.

  • For a person's own individual events, such as birth, death or residence, the Who column is normally empty because it is their page.

  • For family events, such as marriage, the Who column identifies the other partner. For events involving relatives, it identifies the relevant family member.

  • For Participation events, the Who column identifies the principal people associated with the event.

items.title: 7.6.2 Details
items.text:
The Details column identifies other participants and their roles, such as witnesses, clergy or celebrants.

  • A person who has more than one role is listed once, with their additional roles grouped together (for example, Best man, Witness).

  • Additional roles of a primary participant are displayed in Details.

items.title: 7.7 Participation Events
items.text:
An event in which a person does not have a Primary or Family role is displayed as a Participation event. Its event type appears on the first line, with the person’s role or roles on a second line, for example Marriage followed by (:Best man).

Suppose Joan Shakespeare died in November 1646, with Charles Cadbury recorded as a witness and Peter Priestly as the officiating clergy.

The event appears on their respective person pages as follows. The entries all refer to the same Gramps death event; the (:Participation) label makes it clear that the event did not happen to Charles or Peter, but that they were involved in it.

  • Joan Shakespeare’s page: Death event

  • Charles Cadbury’s page: Death (:Witness)

  • Peter Priestly’s page: Death (:Clergy)

The Who column identifies Joan as the principal person on Charles’s and Peter’s pages.

items.title: 7.8 Marriage events
items.text:
Marriage is recorded in Gramps as a Family event rather than as a Person event. The Events table displays marriage and other Family events in the person's timeline. This means it is not necessary to add the same marriage event separately to a person's individual events in Gramps simply to make it appear in their Events display.

Other people associated with the marriage, such as witnesses or celebrants, will have the marriage in their own Events tables as a Participation event.

items.title: 7.9 Maps of Events
items.text:
Maps already existed in DWR. They are available on Person, Family and Place pages when geographical coordinates have been recorded.

  • The Person Map shows locations associated with the person's own events, including marriages and events in which they explicitly participated. Events belonging solely to relatives are excluded.

  • The Family Map shows locations associated with family events and individual events of the parents and children in that family.

  • The Place Map identifies the geographical location of the selected place. It does not show events.

Like DWR, when several events occur at the same coordinates, they are combined into one map marker. Selecting the marker displays the associated people, families and events.

items.title: 7.10 About…
items.text:
Because DWE adds several controls and family events to the original Events display, you can provide an explanation for people using the website.

When creating the report, an optional Gramps note can be selected using Events note on the DWE Options page. If selected, it is displayed in a collapsible About… section on the Events page. If no note is selected, the About section is not displayed.

The note can explain which family events are included, how the display controls work, or anything else that may help people using the website. See About... notes in Chapter 21 DWE Options for information on selecting and using these notes.

items.title: 7.11 Remembering display settings
items.text:
The settings of the check boxes are saved and remembered as you open or reload a page. So, if Siblings is turned off, it is still turned off for the next person you open. Also, if you close a tab, or close the browser, the settings are remembered for next time.

If you already have a couple of person pages open, then changing the settings in one page won’t update the settings of the other opened page, unless/until you reload that other page.

This saved tick behaviour depends on your browser’s local storage settings.

items.title: 8 Lifespans
items.text:
The Lifespans tab provides a graphical view of a person's life in relation to the lives of their immediate family. It makes it easy to see how the person's lifespan overlaps those of their parents, siblings, spouses and children.

The display consists of horizontal lifespan bars arranged against a common time scale. The person whose page is being viewed is the subject of the display.

If you hover over a person’s lifespan bar (or either side of it) their birth and death dates and places are displayed.

Figure 11 - Lifespans chart

items.title: 8.1 People shown
items.text:
The Lifespans display groups people according to their relationship to the subject:

  • Parents

  • Siblings, including the subject

  • Spouses

  • Children

The subject is shown among their siblings, making it easier to see the order and overlap of the children's lives within the family.

A person can belong to more than one family or have more than one set of parents. DWE uses the parent-child relationships recorded in Gramps when finding the people to include and when describing their relationship to the subject. These can include birth, adoptive, foster, step and other parent-child relationships explicitly recorded in Gramps.

A person who occurs more than once as a child of the subject is shown only once in the Lifespans display.

Relatives are grouped by their relationship to the subject rather than by individual family. The Parents & siblings and Spouses & children sections on a person's page can be examined when the individual family structures and recorded relationships need to be viewed in more detail.

Relatives excluded by a selected Person filter at the time the report is created do not appear in the diagram.

items.title: 8.2 Lifespan bars and markers
items.text:
Where both birth and death dates are available, a horizontal bar shows the person's lifespan between the two dates. Birth and death are also indicated by markers on the timescale.

If only a birth date or only a death date is available, a marker is shown for the known date, but no lifespan bar can be drawn. When birth and death are very close together, the markers are displayed in a form that makes them easier to distinguish.

Each person is identified by name and by their relationship to the subject. The different family roles are also distinguished by colour. The colours are shown in a Legend on the right.

items.title: 8.3 Dates and ordering
items.text: Parents, siblings and children are ordered by birth date where available. Spouses are ordered by marriage date where available. People for whom the relevant date is unknown are placed after those with known dates and are still included in the display, rather than being discarded. This allows the chart to remain useful even when some dates in the family tree are incomplete.

items.title: 8.4 Timescale
items.text:
The Lifespans timescale extends from the earliest to the latest date that can be plotted for the people included in the chart. Birth, death and marriage dates affect the extent of the timescale.

To make it easier to compare a person's dates with the timescale and with other lifespans, hover over the person's name. Vertical date hints extending towards the timescale are displayed and change as you move from person to person.

The date hints can be shown or hidden using the Date hints checkbox. The setting is remembered by the browser.

items.title: 8.5 Marriage events
items.text:
Marriage events are shown on the Lifespans display so that marriages can be seen in the same time context as births, deaths and other family members' lifespans. Hover over a marriage marker to display its date and place. The marriage marker is a vertical line joining the two participants, placed at the appropriate date if known.

Figure 12- marriage marker

Marriage events can be shown or hidden using the Marriages checkbox. The setting is remembered by the browser.

Undated marriages

When a marriage is recorded in Gramps but has no usable date, it is displayed in a separate area to the left of the dated timeline. If several undated marriages are present, their connecting lines are spaced horizontally to distinguish them. If there are no undated marriages, the separate area is omitted.

Figure 13- display of an undated marriage

items.title: 8.6 Label height
items.text:
Depending on the size of your screen and the number of people shown in the chart, you may want to adjust the label size to make the chart easier to read.

The Label height slider changes the font size of the person labels. The selected label height is remembered by the browser and is used for other Lifespans charts you view.

Changing the label height does not change the vertical spacing between people.

items.title: 8.7 Moving to another person
items.text: Each person's name in the Lifespans display is a link. Select a name to move to that person's page. Their page opens with the last view you used for that page. You can select their Lifespans tab to see the chart for that person and their family.

items.title: 8.8 Saving the chart
items.text:
The Lifespans chart can be saved as an image. Select the three-dot menu at the upper right of the chart and choose Save as SVG or Save as PNG. The files are named lifespans.svg or lifespans.png and are normally saved in the browser's Downloads folder.

SVG is particularly useful if the chart is to be enlarged, printed or edited later, because it is a vector format and can be resized without losing quality. PNG is convenient for ordinary image use.

items.title: 8.9 About… note
items.text: The website creator can provide an optional note containing information about the Lifespans display. When a Lifespans note has been selected in the DWE Options, it is displayed under About... If no note has been selected, the About section is not shown.

items.title: 9 Citations
items.text:
Citations identify the sources of information recorded in the family tree. If items such as a name or an event have a citation recorded, then DWE displays a citation marker next to that item. Citation markers are highlighted and labelled, for example 1a, 1b, 2a and so on.

The Citations section on a person's page lists all citations associated with that person and the related information displayed on their page. This may include the person, their family, events, media and other references.

The original Dynamic Web Report displayed citations in a list under a Sources section. DWE retains that presentation but renames the section Citations. DWE also adds an alternative searchable table format.

If you click on any citation marker on a webpage then DWE opens the Citations section to display the citation. If the display is in table format, then the row containing that citation is located and highlighted.

The Citations section is displayed if citations are available for the person.

items.title: 9.1 Choosing the display format
items.text:
Visitors can choose whether citations are displayed as the original list or the searchable table. Open the Configuration page, using the gear icon at the top right of the website page, and select Use a table format for individual citations.

Figure 14- Citations format option

When selected, citations are displayed in the searchable table. Clear the checkbox to return to the original list. The selection is remembered by the browser and applies when viewing other individuals.

items.title: 9.2 Original list format
items.text:
The original list displays citations and their associated sources in the DWR format. That presentation is retained for visitors who prefer the familiar layout. It has a compact format.

Figure 15- Citations list

items.title: 9.3 Searchable table format
items.text:
The alternative table format provides a way to find and examine citations, particularly when an individual has many citations.

The table has four columns:

  • Citation — identifies the citation.

  • Source — identifies the source to which the citation belongs.

  • Cited in — identifies where the citation is used on the person's page.

  • Details — displays additional citation information.

If you have reached the table by clicking a citation marker, then that citation row is highlighted.

Figure 16- Citations table

The table can be searched and sorted using its controls.

  • Sort a column by clicking the up/down arrow in the column name.

  • At upper right there is a control to select the column to search, and a control to enter search text. As you enter text the row display reduces, to show only those rows with that text included.

Figure 17- rows filtered by text search

items.title: 9.4 Finding where a citation is used
items.text:
The Cited in column identifies the item associated with a citation.

Select a link in the Cited in column to return to the corresponding citation marker elsewhere on the person's page. If the citation marker is within a closed tab, DWE opens the tab so that the citation marker can be found.

items.title: 9.5 Source scope
items.text: Sources in this section are only those sources for which citations were found for this person. To see all sources included in the generated website, use the Sources Index option on the top-level menu.

items.title: 9.6 About...
items.text:
The website creator may have provided an optional explanatory note for the Citations section.

When supplied, the note appears in an About... panel above the citations. The About section is initially collapsed and can be expanded to read the explanation. If no note has been selected, the About section is not displayed.

See DWE Options for information about creating the Citations note.

items.title: 10 Tree Viewer
items.text:
DWE provides an interactive graphical Tree Viewer for exploring relationships within the family tree. It uses a version of the Topola Genealogy Viewer that is bundled with DWE.

Topola is the tool already used by Gramps to generate the interactive family tree available from the main Gramps menu under Tools → Analysis and Exploration → Interactive Family Tree. Tree Viewer makes that view available to a DWE website visitor.

items.title: 10.1 Tree and Tree Viewer
items.text:
DWE provides two different interactive tree displays:

  • Tree is the family-tree display inherited from the original Dynamic Web Report. It provides extensive configuration options for controlling the content and appearance of the tree. Tree can be opened from the top-level menu bar on any report page.

  • Tree Viewer is the additional DWE display based on Topola. It provides a different way of exploring the family tree, allowing you to navigate through the chart and select people directly from the graphical display. Tree Viewer can be opened by selecting the Tree Viewer tab on a person’s page.

The two displays are independent. Tree is the familiar Dynamic Web Report tree, while Tree Viewer provides another way of navigating and exploring the genealogy data.

Figure 18 Person page showing Tree and Tree Viewer controls

items.title: 10.2 Setup
items.text: Tree Viewer is set up by the DWE website creator. When creating the DWE report, the creator will select the option to include Tree Viewer on the website. See Include Tree Viewer in Chapter 21 of this guide.

items.title: 10.3 Using the Tree Viewer
items.text:
When Tree Viewer is opened, the tree is initially centred on the person whose DWE page you are viewing. That person is highlighted within the tree. A side panel on the right shows details about that person.

Figure 19- Tree Viewer

The Tree Viewer display and controls are very similar to the Gramps Interactive Family Tree display. You can pan and zoom the display and select people in the tree to explore their family relationships. You can collapse the side panel by selecting the → arrow icon at the top of the side panel. Click the icon again to redisplay the panel.

If you select another person in the display, the tree is reorganised and the new person is highlighted. You can also click on a name in the side panel to move to a new person.

As you move around the tree the side panel details change to match the person highlighted in the tree, but you are still within the original person’s DWE page. The side panel contains an Open page for this person button. Selecting the button opens the highlighted person’s DWE page.

The tree is initially displayed within the Tree Viewer section. To give the tree more space, select the Maximize icon at the top right of the Tree Viewer. The viewer expands to fill the browser window, and the button changes to Restore. Select Restore to return to the normal display.

items.title: 10.4 Tree Viewer controls
items.text:
The toolbar across the top of the Tree Viewer provides the standard Topola controls:

  • Print — opens the browser's print facility for printing the displayed family tree.

  • Download — saves the displayed tree as a PDF, PNG or SVG file. The files are named DWEtree.pdf, DWEtree.png and DWEtree.svg, and are normally saved in the browser’s Downloads folder.

  • View — selects the way the family tree is displayed. The available views are described below.

  • Search — searches for a person in the tree. Partial names can be used. Selecting a person from the search results changes the focus of the tree to that person.

  • + and − — zoom in and out.

You can also drag the tree to move around the display.

items.title: 10.5 Choosing the tree view
items.text:
Select View to change the way the family tree is displayed. Four views are available:

  • Hourglass chart — displays ancestors and descendants around the selected person. This is the normal Tree Viewer display.

  • All relatives — displays a wider range of people related to the selected person.

  • Donatso family chart — provides an alternative graphical arrangement of the family.

  • Family tree (experimental) — displays people graphically on a drawing of a tree. This view is most practical when displaying a relatively small number of people.

The selected view is not remembered when you leave the Tree Viewer. When you open the Tree Viewer again, it starts with the Hourglass chart.

items.title: 10.6 Tree Viewer data
items.text:
When Tree Viewer is enabled Tree Viewer and the data it requires are automatically created. A website visitor does not need to install Topola, visit the Topola website, or provide a separate GEDCOM file

  • DWE generates a GEDCOM file containing the genealogical data required by the viewer.

  • DWE removes the Gramps researcher copyright information from the GEDCOM.

  • That file and a bundled Topola viewer with its supporting files are placed in the generated website.

The GEDCOM file generated for the Tree Viewer respects the Person filter selected when creating the DWE report, including custom filters. Individuals excluded by the filter are not exported to the GEDCOM, and relationships that depend on those individuals may therefore be absent from the tree.

For example, if a filter excludes a person's ancestors, their siblings may still appear in the Tree Viewer but may not be connected through their excluded parents.

items.title: 10.7 About...
items.text: The website creator can provide an optional note containing information about the Tree Viewer. When a Tree Viewer note has been selected in DWE Options, it is displayed under About... in the Tree Viewer section. If no note has been selected, the About section is not shown.

items.title: 11 Tracking
items.text:
Tracking shows how people in the DWE website are related to one or more selected people. It can be useful when exploring a large family tree, because it provides a quick indication of how the person you are viewing connects to people whose relationship to you is already familiar.

For example, you might track yourself and your partner, or several people representing different branches of the family. In my family tree I track four people — my two parents and my partner’s two parents. When exploring my partner’s side of the family, this makes it easy to see how people are related to her parents.

DWE uses a Gramps tag to identify the people to be tracked. You can track as many people as you wish, or not use Tracking at all.

items.title: 11.1 Set up
items.text: Tracking is set up by the DWE website creator. When creating the DWE report, the creator will select a tag as the Tracking tag value. See Tracking tag in Chapter 21 of this guide.

items.title: 11.2.1 Tracked relatives listed on the home page
items.text:
When Tracking is enabled, the people in the report who have the Tracking tag set for them are listed as Tracked relatives on the DWE home page.

Figure 20- no tracked person found

If no Tracking tag has been selected, the section is not displayed.

If a Tracking tag has been selected but no people in the report have that tag, the Tracked relatives section displays a message to alert the website visitor.

items.title: 11.2.2 Tracking entry on a person’s page
items.text:
On a person page, the Tracking entry shows their connection to each tracked person. If the person is related to more than one tracked person, a separate entry is shown for each tracked relative.

The tracked person’s name is a link. Select their name to open their DWE page.

A tracked person won’t show as being related to themselves, but their relationships to other tracked people will still be shown.

Figure 21- Tracking of William Shakespeare shows Judith is a stepdaughter

items.title: 12 Why Me
items.text:
☐ For creators ☑ For visitors

People can be included in a family tree for many reasons. They may be relatives, but may also be other people like friends and neighbours who are important to the family history, though not related.

Why Me provides a way for the website to explain why a particular person is included in the tree. The explanation is stored as a Gramps note attached to that person and is displayed with the person's details on their DWE person page.

Why Me is independent of Tracking. Tracking uses the Gramps relationship calculator to show a person's genealogical relationship to selected tracked people. Why Me is information supplied by the creator of the family tree. A person can therefore have a Tracking relationship, a Why Me note, both, or neither.

items.title: 12.1 Set up
items.text: Why Me is set up by the DWE website creator. When creating the DWE report, the creator will select a Gramps note type as the Why Me note type. See Why me note type in Chapter 21 of this guide.

items.title: 12.2 Result
items.text:
If a person has a note of the selected type, its contents are displayed as Why me in the person's details.

Figure 22- Why me note display on person page

The Why Me note is a Gramps note and will also appear within the person's Notes tab. The Notes tab will be displayed if the website creator has selected the Export Notes option on the Privacy page of the report’s options. That option is inherited from the Dynamic Web Report.

The Why me label can be changed using DWE's Local Labels feature, described in Chapter 15. For example, a website creator might replace the short Why me label with a longer explanation appropriate to the website.

I use Why Me notes for many people in my own tree, including people for whom Tracking relationships are also available. The two features provide different information: Tracking describes a calculated relationship, while Why Me explains why I have included the person in the tree.

items.title: 13 Story
items.text:
☐ For creators ☑ For visitors

The Story feature provides a place for a short introduction or summary, displayed with the person's details near the top of their page.

Story is set up by the DWE website creator. When creating the DWE report, the creator can select a Gramps note type as the Story note type. See Story note type in Chapter 21 of this guide.

items.title: 13.1 Result
items.text:
If a person has a note of the selected type, its contents are displayed as Story in the person's details. If the person does not have a Story note, the Story entry is not displayed.

Figure 23- Story note display

Story notes are ordinary Gramps notes and will also appear with the person's notes in the Notes tab.

I keep Story notes fairly short — only a few sentences. Their purpose is to provide a quick introduction to the person rather than a complete biography. A long Story requires the visitor to scroll past it before reaching the other information on the person's page.

For longer stories, I prefer to create a separate document. For example, I use Microsoft Word's document features, including headings and images, save the finished document as a PDF, and add the PDF to Gramps as media. It can then be linked to the person in the same way as other media.

items.title: 14 Clarifying multiple families
items.text:
☑ For creators ☑ For visitors

The original Dynamic Web Report can show people who belong to more than one family and can display the parent-child relationships recorded in Gramps. However, I found that some less usual family arrangements could be difficult to follow, particularly when several parent families and their children were displayed together.

DWE retains this information but changes parts of its presentation to make the family connections clearer.

items.title: 14.1 Parents & siblings
items.text:
The Parents & siblings tab, called Ancestors in the original Dynamic Web Report, shows the families in which the person is recorded as a child. The display nests children in their appropriate parent family, making it easier to see which people belong to each family. Collapsing a family also collapses its children.

Family type is displayed (such as married or unknown) and parent-child relationships are named. DWE uses the relationships recorded in Gramps and does not try to infer a step relationship from the surrounding family structure.

items.title: 14.2 Children from other families of the parents
items.text:
By default, DWE also shows children from other families of the person's parents. This makes half-sibling relationships and other family connections easier to understand.

For example, if a person's mother has children in another family, that family can also be shown in Parents & siblings, even though the person whose page is being viewed is not a child in that family. DWE makes this clear with the message:

The person on the page is not a child in this family

(This family is another marriage/union of a parent)

The report option Include children from other families of the parents controls this behaviour. It is selected by default in DWE. The option appears on the report’s Advanced options page. Clear the checkbox if you want Parents & siblings to show only the families in which the person is recorded as a child.

This option affects only the Parents & siblings display. Other parts of DWE continue to use the relationships recorded in the family tree. For example, Tracking may identify someone as a half-sibling, and Events may include events for that half-sibling, even when the other family has been hidden by clearing this option.

items.title: 14.3 Families without recorded parents
items.text:
Sometimes you may have discovered that two people are siblings without knowing the identity of either parent. Gramps allows the children to be placed together in a family without adding a father or mother.

DWE can display families without parents in Parents & siblings, allowing the known sibling relationship to be shown without requiring an artificial unknown parent to be created.

Figure 24- family without parents

items.title: 14.4 Spouses & children
items.text: The Spouses & children tab, called Descendants in the original Dynamic Web Report, shows the person's families as a spouse or partner and the children in those families. DWE adds the marriage or family relationship type to the family display.

items.title: 15 Local Labels
items.text:
☑ For creators ☐ For visitors

DWE allows the website creator to replace labels used in the generated report without editing the program code. This can be useful if you prefer different terminology or want labels that are more appropriate for a particular family history website.

items.title: 15.1 Setup
items.text:
Local Labels is set up by the DWE website creator. When creating the DWE report, the creator will select a specific Gramps note as the Local labels note. See Local labels note in Chapter 21 of this guide.

Local Labels are chosen by the person creating the report. Website visitors cannot change the labels themselves.

items.title: 16 About page for website
items.text:
☑ For creators ☐ For visitors

The DWE top level menu has an About page that displays version details, for diagnostic purposes. It also includes a link to a built-in quick guide. The guide can be edited

Figure 25- example About page

items.title: 16.1 Quick guide
items.text:
The Quick guide is a webpage whose content is stored in a separate file distributed with the website. The website creator, or anyone with access to the generated website files, can edit its contents without regenerating the report.

Visitors can open the Quick guide from a hyperlink on the website's About page.

Note that DWE retains the existing Custom Page facility from the Gramps Dynamic Web Report (DWR). Custom Page allows the website creator to add one or more pages to their website menus using content from Gramps notes. The Custom Page facility is described in the DWR documentation on the Gramps wiki.

items.title: 16.2 Key difference – Quick guide and Custom pages
items.text:
DWE now has two complementary ways of adding formatted content to a website:

  • Custom pages – sourced from Gramps notes, edit the notes and regenerate the report to see changes;

  • Quick guide – source is an external file, edit the file and refresh the browser to see changes

A more detailed comparison is shown below:

Custom pages Quick guide From a Gramps note From a Markdown file Are included in the website's navigation menus Accessed through a hyperlink on the About menu page Content is maintained inside Gramps Content is maintained in a file within the website folders Content can include plain text, HTML, Gramps text styling and Markdown Content styling can include plain text and Markdown formatting Changes require editing the Gramps notes in Gramps and regenerating the report Changes require only editing and saving the accessible Markdown file Useful for genealogy-related content Useful for website instructions and visitor information

items.title: 16.3 Key difference – Quick guide and DWE User guide
items.text: The Quick guide is an editable guide for visitors to a generated website, whereas the DWE User Guide is a comprehensive guide that documents the DWE for visitors and website creators.

items.title: 16.4 Editing
items.text:
The Quick guide is an editable Markdown file (quick_guide.md) in the website's main directory. It can be edited by anybody who has access to it. Its contents are converted to HTML whenever the Quick Guide page is opened. The file may contain ordinary plain text or Markdown formatting, including headings, lists, hyperlinks and tables.

When a website is first generated, DWE copies its internal default text (quick_guide_default.md) into the website directory as quick_guide.md. Thereafter the website creator can edit quick_guide.md at any time to customise the guide. A visitor just needs to reload the page in their browser to see the new version.

If you later regenerate the website into the same directory, your edited quick guide file is not overwritten.

items.title: 16.5 Publishing
items.text: If the website is published to a remote server, changes might be made directly to the remote server's copy by the site manager. Care should therefore be taken when uploading a regenerated website to avoid overwriting edits made on the server. If the website is copied to another computer, the same caveat applies.

items.title: 17 Website Themes
items.text:
☐ For creators ☑ For visitors

The look of the website is created using the theme selected by the report creator when generating the report. See section 21.12 Website themes.

A site visitor can change the appearance of the website at any time by selecting another theme on the DWE Configuration page. Open the Configuration page by selecting the gear icon at the top right of a site page.

Two appearance options are available to change themes and borders:

Figure 26- website themes and enhanced borders

items.title: 17.1 Selecting a theme
items.text:
Seven themes are listed:

Default, Mainz, Cerulean, Flatly, Journal, Readable and United.

To change the theme, select the preferred theme from the Website theme dropdown list, and click OK. The website will reload using the selected theme.

The selected theme is remembered by the browser and will normally be used on subsequent visits to the website.

The new themes are from Bootswatch. See the Bootswatch web site for more information on each theme.

Note: If you just want to change any setting on the Configuration page then change it and click the OK button. The Restore default settings, followed by OK restores all the Configuration settings to their defaults, if you ever want to do that.

items.title: 17.2 Enhanced borders
items.text:
The Enhanced borders option on the Configuration page makes the boundaries around sections, tables and tabs more prominent. This can improve readability, particularly with themes that use subtle borders.

To enable this option, select the Enhanced borders checkbox and click OK. The website will reload with stronger borders. To turn off enhanced borders deselect Enhanced borders (no tick showing) followed by OK.

The setting is independent of the selected website theme and is remembered by the browser in the same way as the theme selection.

items.title: 17.3 Local server limitation
items.text:
Note for visitors running a local web server: If the website is opened using a local server that selects a different port each time it starts, the browser may not remember the previously selected theme and the Enhaced borders setting.

The View report locally.bat feature (see section 5.8 Local viewing) is set up to use a different port each time it starts. In this case, the website will open using the report creator's default theme, and the visitor will need to select their preferred theme again.

items.title: 18 Statistics
items.text:
☐ For creators ☑ For visitors

Dynamic Web Extended includes a Statistics menu containing two pages:

  • Metrics —nothing is shown yet, it is reserved for future development.

  • Notable records — displays interesting genealogical records calculated from the family tree. It is based on the Gramps Records gramplet.

The Statistics menus are only displayed if the website creator has enables Statistics. See section 21.4 Include Statistics.

items.title: 18.1 Notable records
items.text:
Select Statistics → Notable records from the website menu.

The page identifies individuals and families associated with notable events and characteristics, such as:

  • Lifespans: People who died at the youngest or oldest ages.

  • Marriage: People who married or divorced at the youngest or oldest ages, and those with the most marriages.

  • Children: Individuals with the most children or grandchildren, and families with the most children.

The available results depend on the information recorded in the family tree. Some categories may have no qualifying records.

items.title: 18.2 Viewing and selecting records
items.text:
The page initially displays the selected records in each category, on the left. It displays the categories in a navigation menu on the right.

Figure 27- notable records lists

items.title: 18.3 Number of records to show
items.text:
Visitors can change the number displayed in each category using the Number to show field at the top of the page. Enter a whole number between 1 and 100, then press Enter or move to another field to update the display.

The new number is remembered when navigating between pages and when returning to the website using the same browser.

items.title: 18.4 Selecting a category
items.text:
The Jump to category navigation list at the side provides fast access to categories; click the browser back button to go back to the top.

When you select a category its category name is highlighted, making it easier to see that category.

Each result includes a linked individual or family name and the corresponding record value (such as number of children). Select a name to open its details page.

items.title: 18.5 Ranking and tied records
items.text:
Records are ordered by their values, with the highest or lowest values first, as appropriate for the category. Where records have equal values, they are listed alphabetically.

If several records are tied at the cutoff, all tied records are displayed, instead of leaving some of them out. Consequently, a category may show more results than the number selected.

items.title: 18.6 Privacy and filtering
items.text:
Notable records are calculated using the individuals and families included in the generated website.

The calculations respect the report's filtering, privacy and living-person settings. Consequently, the results may differ from records calculated using the complete Gramps family tree.

items.title: 18.7 Interpreting the results
items.text:
The records depend on the completeness and accuracy of the information entered in Gramps. For example, ages at marriage or parenthood require sufficient date information to calculate them.

The Person with most marriages category is new and counts distinct families with a Marriage or Alternate Marriage event. Multiple qualifying marriage events associated with the same family are counted as one marriage.

The results provide an interesting way to explore the family tree.

items.title: 19 Calendar
items.text:
☐ For creators ☑ For visitors

Dynamic Web Extended (DWE) provides an interactive Calendar that displays birth, marriage and death events from the family history. It displays 12 months of the year, typically in a 3 by 4 grid, depending on the width of the browser. The calendar groups events by month and day, regardless of the historical year in which they occurred.

The Calendar is based on the Web Calendar report that is also available in Gramps, and has been updated and modified to work with DWE.

The Calendar is an online display and does not provide a printing facility. Other Gramps reports and addons are available for creating printed calendars if required.

items.title: 19.1 Calendar display
items.text:
The Calendar is an option when the report is generated, and can be opened through the top-level Calendar menu:

The website creator has previously determined which event types and historical years are included in the Calendar.

Each month displays its dates arranged under weekday headings. Dates that have events show a number indicating how many events are recorded for that month and day.

Figure 28- Calendar display

The Calendar uses the current year to set the weekday positions of dates. Consequently, the weekday shown for an event does not necessarily correspond to the weekday on which the historical event occurred.

items.title: 19.2 Viewing events
items.text:
Events are listed with the most recent year first.

Visitors can examine events associated with a date in two ways:

  • Hover over a date to see a temporary preview of the events.

  • Click a date to open a popup that remains visible, allowing the visitor to examine the events and follow links to Individual pages.

This image shows hover over date; there is only one event on this date. This event has a description.

Figure 29- Hover over date

items.title: 19.2.1 Events with an unknown day
items.text: Events with a known month but an unknown day are grouped under an asterisk (*) in the bottom-right cell of the relevant month. Hovering over or clicking the asterisk displays these events in the same way as events associated with a particular date.

items.title: 19.2.2 29<sup>th</sup> February
items.text: The Calendar includes 29 February every year, even when the current year is not a leap year. This ensures that events recorded on 29 February remain visible.

items.title: 19.3.1 Living people only / All people
items.text:
The Calendar provides two options for controlling which events are displayed.

  • Living people only – displays events associated with people considered probably living.

  • All people – displays all events, subject to the report's filtering and privacy settings.

Changing the selection immediately updates the event counts and the events displayed.

A person without a recorded death date is not necessarily considered living. Gramps uses available information and its probable-living rules when determining whether someone is likely to be alive.

These options do not change the information included in the generated website.

items.title: 19.3.2 Today button
items.text: The Today button scrolls the Calendar to the current date.

items.title: 19.4 About section
items.text:
The website creator may provide an optional explanatory note for the Calendar. The note appears in an expandable About... section above the Calendar heading and controls.

The section can be expanded or collapsed. Its state is preserved when switching between Living people only and All people.

items.title: 19.5 How dates are handled
items.text: The Calendar uses the month and day recorded for an event, rather than the historical year, to determine where it appears. Only events within the year range specified by the website creator are included.

items.title: 19.5.1 Dates included
items.text:
The following dates are included in a Calendar:

  • Exact dates — Dates with a known day, month and year.

  • Month-only dates — Dates with a known month and year but no known day.

  • About dates — Approximate dates with a known month.

  • Estimated dates — Estimated dates with a known month.

  • Calculated dates — Calculated dates with a known month.

For About, Estimated and Calculated dates, events with a known day appear on that date. Events with a known month but an unknown day appear under the asterisk (*) for that month.

items.title: 19.5.2 Dates excluded
items.text:
The following dates are excluded:

  • Year-only dates, where the month is unknown.

  • Empty or unknown dates without usable month information.

  • Dates qualified as Before or After.

  • Dates qualified as From or To.

  • Date ranges and date spans.

These restrictions prevent dates with uncertain boundaries from being displayed as specific calendar dates.

items.title: 19.6 Privacy and filtering
items.text:
Calendar events are subject to the report creator's selected Gramps filters and privacy settings. Visitors cannot use the Calendar to access individuals or events excluded from the generated report. Selecting All people does not override these restrictions.

For information about configuring the Calendar, see chapter 22 Calendar Options in the report creator section of this guide.

items.title: 19.7 Married names
items.text: The website creator can decide to use a woman’s own name or her married name when including birthday events for women. Thus, her name might be different in different events. See also section 23.19 Birthday surname.

items.title: 20 Other enhancements
items.text:
DWE includes several smaller changes in addition to the features described elsewhere in this guide.

  • Home page categories — The categories on the DWE home page are presented in a table to make the list easier to read.

  • Table page sizes — DWE adds 20 to the choices available in the Show Entries selector on table pages, providing an intermediate choice between 10 and 50 entries.

  • Person Index sorting — The Person Index can be displayed as either a table or a list. In table view, the columns can be sorted using the sort controls in the column headings. In list view, sorting is controlled by the Sort by selector. DWE adds choices for sorting by birth or death date with either the earliest or latest dates first.

  • Dates — Hyphens within dates are non-breaking, so a date won’t split across two lines.

  • Life span — The original DWR displays a person's Age at death in their person-page details. DWE also displays their Life span, showing the period from birth to death. When both are available, Age at death and Life span are displayed together on the same row.

  • Remembering the tabbed-panel setting — The Configuration page includes an option to display information using either tabbed panels or separate linear sections. DWE now remembers the visitor's selection, when navigating between individuals and other pages, and when returning to the website in a later browser session. The selection remains in effect until it is changed in Configuration.

  • Searching for people – The name search includes nicknames recorded in both primary and alternative names. You can search using a nickname alone or combine it with a surname.

  • Configuration page – The Configuration page is inherited from the original DWR. It allows website visitors to change how information is displayed. DWE retains this functionality and introduces some additional settings. The DWE enhancements include:

    • Website themes: Visitors can select a different theme for the website. See the Website Themes chapter.

    • Theme border enhancement: page panel and table borders are easier to see.

    • Citation table display: Visitors can choose between list and table views for citations. See the Citations chapter.

    • These enhancements are described in their respective chapters. The other Configuration page settings are inherited from DWR and are not described separately in this guide.

items.title: 21 DWE Options
items.text:
☑ For creators ☐ For visitors

For the website creator, Dynamic Web Extended adds a DWE Options page to the report options. This page brings together the settings for features added by DWE. Options inherited unchanged from the Dynamic Web Report (for example the Privacy options) remain on their normal option pages and are not described in this Guide.

Figure 30- DWE Options

items.title: 21.1 Option defaults and saved settings
items.text:
When creating a DWE report for a family tree for the first time, DWE provides initial values for its options. Gramps saves the options. If you change them, they are reused the next time you create a DWE report for that family tree. Each family tree therefore has its own saved report settings.

*Notes used only to configure DWE can conveniently be attached to a specially created dummy person in the tree, such as a person named ‘Gramps’. This prevents them from appearing as unused objects when Gramps database repair or checking tools are used. Examples include the Tree Viewer, Events, Lifespans, Parent-child relationship and Local labels notes.

The initial settings for a new family tree are:

DWE option Initial setting Tracking tag Empty Include Tree Viewer Selected Tree Viewer note Empty Events note Empty Lifespans note Empty Citations note Empty Parent-child relationship note Empty Local labels note Empty Why Me note type Empty Story note type Empty Use Markdown note marker Selected Markdown note type Empty Treat ordinary notes as Markdown Not selected

items.title: 21.2 Tracking tag
items.text:
The Tracking tag identifies the tag to be used when DWE calculates Tracking relationships. Tracking shows the connection of each person in the report to the tracked individual or individuals.

DWE tracking uses a Gramps tag. Instructions on how to create and manage Gramps tags are provided in the Gramps Wiki Manual.

See Chapter 11 Tracking for a description of the information displayed by this feature.

items.title: 21.2.1 Create a Gramps tag
items.text:
Select Edit → Tag → New Tag from the Gramps top menu. Create or choose a Gramps tag to identify the people you want to track. The tag can have any name; for example, you might call it ‘Track me’. You can use an existing tag.

Figure 31- create a tracking tag

items.title: 21.2.2 Set the Tracking tag value
items.text:
Select an existing tag in the Tracking tag option.

Figure 32 - select the tag to be used

Tracking is optional. To turn it off, select the blank entry for Tracking tag before generating the report again. If the option is left empty, Tracking entries are not generated.

items.title: 21.2.3 Assign the Tracking tag
items.text:
In the Gramps person editor, for each person you want to be tracked, select the Tag button and assign the ‘Track me’ tag to that person.

For example, you might assign that tag to William Shakespeare.

Figure 33- apply tagging on the Person Editor page

The Tracking entry on a person's page can then show their relationship to William Shakespeare, such as son, sister or wife. The web page for Susanna Shakespeare would show this Tracking entry:

items.title: 21.3 Include Tree Viewer
items.text:
Select Include Tree Viewer to include an interactive Tree Viewer in the generated website.

When this option is selected, DWE adds a Tree Viewer tab to the website's person pages and automatically generates the GEDCOM file required by this viewer.

Clear the checkbox if the Tree Viewer is not required.

Warning — Tree Viewer performance with large family trees

The Tree Viewer uses the Topola genealogy viewer, which may have difficulty displaying large or complex family trees. In some cases, the tree may fail to render, and the browser may become unresponsive.

During testing, a family tree containing approximately 1,100 people displayed correctly, while a test tree containing approximately 4,600 people failed to render and caused the browser to become unresponsive.

The same behaviour was observed in Gramps' Tools → Analysis and Exploration → Interactive Family Tree, which also uses Topola.

These observations do not establish a fixed maximum tree size. Performance may also depend on the structure and complexity of the family tree.

Recommendation: Before enabling Tree Viewer in DWE, test your family tree using Gramps' Interactive Family Tree tool. If it does not display correctly there, it may also fail in DWE.

See Chapter 10 Tree Viewer for more information about using this feature.

items.title: 21.4 Include Statistics
items.text:
This option will display a top level Statistics menu with two selections:

  • The Metrics selection has no content at present.

  • The Notable records selection displays lists of categories such as longest-lived person, person with most marriages, most children and similar.

See chapter 18 Statistics for more information.

items.title: 21.5 About... notes
items.text:
These options all use the same DWE About note concept.

An About note is an optional Gramps note containing information that the website creator wants to provide to visitors for each of these features. Its contents are displayed in a collapsible/expandable About... section above the main content. To collapse or expand the note a user can click the chevron icon to the right of the About title bar.

The text is displayed from the note, and the note can say whatever you want, in whatever language you need. An About note might explain how to use the feature and what information can be seen. Example About notes are provided in the Appendix.

The features themselves do not require an About note. Leaving the corresponding option empty simply means that there is no About note, and an About box will not be displayed.

items.title: 21.5.1 Tree Viewer note
items.text: Select an optional Gramps note to provide the About note for the Tree Viewer display.

items.title: 21.5.2 Events note
items.text: Select an optional Gramps note to provide the About note for the Events display.

items.title: 21.5.3 Lifespans note
items.text: Select an optional Gramps note to provide the About note for the Lifespans display.

items.title: 21.5.4 Citations note
items.text: Select an optional Gramps note to provide the About note for the Citations display.

items.title: 21.6 Parent-child relationship note
items.text:
Gramps records the relationship of a child to each parent in the family, for example Birth or Adopted. DWE extends that to name the relationship in both directions — from a parent to a child and from a child to a parent. The extended relationship phrases are used for wording in the Events tables and in the Lifespans charts.

The optional Parent-child relationship note allows the website creator to override the default terms. If you don’t need to change the defaults, you don’t need a note.

Each relationship is placed on a separate line of the note. A line has 5 fields separated by ‘>’:

Pattern for parent-child note:

Gramps name > parent phrase > child phrase > kinship position > optional comment

The first field is the Gramps relationship name.

The second is the phrase used for the parent relationship and

the third is the phrase used for the child relationship.

The fourth field controls whether DWE should add the appropriate kinship term, such as father, mother, parent, son, daughter or child. It can take these values:

Value Meaning A Add the kinship term after the relationship phrase P Add the kinship term before the relationship phrase blank Do not add a kinship term

The fifth field is an optional comment about the line.

items.title: 21.6.1 Example phrases
items.text:
This example:

Adopted > adopting > adopted > A

can produce adopting father and adopted son

Using P instead:

Adopted > adopting > adopted > P

can produce father adopting and son adopted. This provides flexibility for languages in which a different word order is appropriate.

Phrase fields can deliberately be left empty:

Birth > > > A

This means that only the kinship term is displayed, such as father, mother, son or daughter

Anything after the fourth field is ignored by DWE and can therefore be used as a comment:

Birth > > > A > Appends the kinship term to the default relationship type

items.title: 21.6.2 Using relationship substitutions
items.text: The optional note does not need to replace the entire set of defaults. A line in the note overrides the wording for that relationship. Relationships not mentioned in the note continue to use their built-in defaults.

items.title: 21.6.3 Other Languages
items.text: The note feature works with other languages. For example, instead of ‘Birth’ The note for a French locale would start with ‘Naissance’, followed by the parent and child phrases, and the A and P option if required.

items.title: 21.7 Local labels note
items.text:
The Local labels note allows some labels used in the generated website to be replaced with wording chosen by the website creator.

This is useful where different terminology is preferred for a particular family history, or where a more explanatory label is wanted without modifying DWE itself. If you don’t need different terminology, you don’t need a note.

Select the Gramps note containing the required label definitions. If the option is left empty, the normal DWE labels are used.

items.title: 21.7.1 Creating a Local Labels note
items.text:
Create a Gramps note. It can be of any type, although General is probably a useful choice.

Each label replacement is entered on a separate line in the form:

existing label > replacement label

For example:

Why me > Why is this person in the tree?

The label on the left must exactly match the existing DWE label. The > character separates the existing and replacement labels.

Lines that do not contain the separator are ignored. They can therefore be used for comments or a description of the notes. Putting a description on the first line of the note can also make the note easier to recognise when selecting it from a list of Gramps notes.

In my Local labels note the first line, a comment line, starts with a dash for convenience, so it is sorted towards the top of the note lists when I look for it later.

items.title: 21.7.2 Selecting the note
items.text:
When creating the report, select the required note using the Local labels note selector on the DWE Options page.

Figure 34- note selector

Generate the report and the specified labels will be replaced.

The changes do not alter the original DWE labels in the DWE code or the information stored in Gramps. To stop using the replacements, clear the Local labels note selection and generate the report again.

items.title: 21.7.3 Scope of a replacement
items.text:
A Local Labels replacement applies wherever DWE uses the translated label. It is not restricted to a particular page or tab. Care should therefore be taken when replacing a label that may be used in several places.

Local Labels operate on the labels in the language used to generate the report. This means replacements can also be used with translated DWE reports.

items.title: 21.7.4 Example
items.text:
For example, DWE uses Parents & siblings and Spouses & children for the two person-page tabs that the original Dynamic Web Report named Ancestors and Descendants. If you prefer the original terminology, Local Labels can restore it:

Parents & siblings > Ancestors
Spouses & children > Descendants

The DWE display changes:

Figure 35- without local labels

Figure 36- after local labels

items.title: 21.8 Note types to enhance the person page
items.text: The next two note types identify a type of note. If a person has a note of that type in their Gramps record, then the content of the note is displayed specially in the top section of their website page. The note types to be identified are the Why me note type and Story note type.
