items.title: 21.9 Why me note type
items.text: The Why me note type identifies notes that DWE should put into the Why Me information displayed for a person.

items.title: 21.9.1 Create Why Me note type
items.text:
You can create a custom note type specifically for this purpose. In my tree I use a custom note type named Why Me, but you can use any note type you prefer.

Select that note type in the DWE option for Why me note type. Why me is optional; if no note type is selected, then Why Me is not shown.

items.title: 21.9.2 Add Why me notes
items.text:
Prior to generating the DWE report, in your Gramps database you will need to create a Gramps note for a person and attach it to the person. Set the note to the type selected for the Why Me note type.

Attach the note to the person using the Notes tab in their Person Editor. You can share a note between persons if appropriate or create a different note for each person.

items.title: 21.9.3 Result
items.text:
DWE finds that note type in a person’s data when the report is generated by the creator. The DWE website will display the note in the Why me entry on the person’s website page.

See Why Me for further explanation.

items.title: 21.10 Story note type
items.text:
The Story note type identifies the notes used for the short Story displayed near the top of a person's page.

The Story note type option is very similar to the Why Me note type option described above. You can create a custom note type specifically for this purpose. In my tree I use a custom note type called Story, but you can use any note type you prefer.

A person with a note of that type will then have it displayed as their Story on their website person page.

If no Story note exists for a person, the Story is not displayed. Story is optional. To turn it off, select the blank entry for Story note type before generating the report again.

See Story for further information.

items.title: 21.11 Markdown in notes
items.text:
DWE can render Markdown contained in Gramps notes. There are three ways of identifying notes that should be treated as Markdown. These methods can be used separately or together.

DWE first preserves the normal Gramps styling in a note and then applies Markdown processing. This makes it possible, for example, to add a Markdown table to a note that also contains Gramps formatting such as bold, underline or subscript.

Because this combines two formatting systems, unusual combinations of Gramps styling and Markdown should be checked in the generated report.

items.title: 21.11.1 Use Markdown note marker
items.text:
When Use Markdown note marker is selected, an individual note can be identified as Markdown by putting:

MD

by itself on the first line.

DWE recognises this as its Markdown marker and while converting the note it removes the marker from the displayed note. The note can be of any type, except Html code and To Do.

The MD marker is a fixed DWE convention. The option determines whether DWE recognises the marker; it does not change the marker itself.

This option is selected initially. It can be turned off if you don’t want to use the MD marker method.

items.title: 21.11.2 Markdown note type
items.text:
The Markdown note type provides another way to identify Markdown notes.

Select a Gramps note type that is to be used for Markdown. Eligible notes of that type are then processed as Markdown without requiring an MD marker on each note.

This can be convenient when Markdown notes are maintained as a distinct type in the Gramps database.

items.title: 21.11.3 Treat ordinary notes as Markdown
items.text:
Selecting Treat ordinary notes as Markdown applies Markdown processing more generally. Ordinary notes can then contain Markdown without needing either the MD marker or the selected Markdown note type.

The three methods therefore provide different levels of control: the marker can identify individual notes, a note type can identify a group of notes, and this option can apply Markdown processing generally.

Gramps Html code and To Do notes are excluded from DWE Markdown processing. Their note types take precedence over all three Markdown methods. For example, an Html code note is not processed as Markdown even if its first line contains the MD marker.

items.title: 21.12 Website themes
items.text:
The Report options page allows the site creator to affect the appearance of the site using the Web site template option. In this guide website templates are called website themes.

Figure 37- website option

The original DWR provided two options, named Default and Mainz. DWE has increased the number of options. To select a new theme, select its name from the dropdown list.

The theme selected in Gramps determines the initial appearance of the website, but with DWE visitors can subsequently choose a different theme. Their view of the site will change to match their newly selected theme. The visitor option is described in section 17 Website Theme

The new themes are from Bootswatch, a free, open-source collection of themes that change the visual appearance of the Bootstrap front-end framework used inside DWR and DWE. See the Bootswatch site for more information.

items.title: 21.13 Short name option
items.text: DWE inherits a Short Name Format option on the Report options page, to use for person names in parts of the report. The short name is used in the top-level menu Tree when that tree is displayed. DWE also uses the short name in the new one-line heading section of a person page.

items.title: 22 Calendar Options
items.text:
☑ For creators ☐ For visitors

DWE adds a Calendar Options tab to the report’s options tabs. It defines the Calendar page included in a DWE website. The calendar displays days of the year, and for each day it can show the events that occurred on that day.

The Calendar is optional.

  • The website creator determines which event types are included, the historical year range, and some other display settings.

  • Visitors can explore the events included in the generated website but cannot change the creator's configuration.

Figure 38- Calendar options

items.title: 22.1 Include calendar
items.text: Enables the Calendar page in the generated website. When this option is disabled, the Calendar page is omitted from the generated website, and the remaining calendar-specific options are disabled.

items.title: 22.2 First day of week
items.text:
Determines which weekday appears at the beginning of each calendar week.

The Calendar uses the current year to determine the weekday positions of dates, independently of the selected first day of the week.

items.title: 22.3 Birthday surname
items.text:
This option determines which surname is displayed for women in Calendar birth entries. This option does not affect the surname displayed for men.

  • Own surname — Uses the woman's own primary name as recorded in Gramps.

  • Husband's surname (first family) — Uses the surname of the husband in her first listed family.

  • Husband's surname (last family) — Uses the surname of the husband in her last listed family.

First and last family refer to the order of families recorded in Gramps, not necessarily the chronological order of marriages.

If a woman has a Married name recorded in Gramps, that name takes precedence over the selected husband's surname.

The husband's surname is taken from his primary name in Gramps when the report is generated. If the selected family or husband is unavailable, the woman's own primary name is used.

This option applies only to birth entries. Marriage and death entries use the individuals' primary names.

items.title: 22.4 Event inclusion
items.text:
Three options determine which event types are included:

  • Include birthdays — Include birth events.

  • Include marriages — Include marriage events.

  • Include death dates — Include death events.

The options can be selected independently. Only the selected event types are exported to the Calendar.

items.title: 22.5 Calendar year range
items.text:
Two options determine the range of historical event years included in the Calendar:

  • Show data from start of year

    • The earliest year to include

    • defaults to the current year minus the Gramps maximum probable living age, as defined in the Gramps configuration.

  • Show data to end of year

    • The latest year to include

    • defaults to the current year.

Both boundary years are included.

For example, setting the starting year to 1850 and the ending year to 1950 includes eligible events dated from 1 January 1850 through 31 December 1950.

items.title: 22.5.1 Default year range
items.text:
Year values can be changed to include earlier historical events or future-dated events.

If new year values are entered then Gramps remembers the change the next time the report options are opened, it does not replace them with the defaults.

items.title: 22.5.2 Year-range validation
items.text:
The starting year must not be later than the ending year.

If the starting year exceeds the ending year, DWE displays an error message and does not generate the report until the range is corrected.

items.title: 22.5.3 Relationship to the living-person filter
items.text:
The year range determines which events are included in the generated Calendar.

The visitor's Living people only / All people selection determines which of those events are displayed.

These are independent filters.

For example, a person born in 1850 with no recorded death date may be excluded from the Living people only display because Gramps considers the person unlikely to be alive, even though their birth event falls within the configured year range.

items.title: 22.6 Calendar note
items.text:
The Calendar note option allows the website creator to select an existing Gramps note containing explanatory information about the Calendar.

When a note is selected and contains text, it is displayed in an expandable About... section above the Calendar heading.

The note supports DWE's existing Gramps text formatting and Markdown processing.

If no note is selected, the About section is omitted.

The website creator can use the note to explain the Calendar's purpose, the information included, or any conventions specific to the family history. An example Calendar Note is included in the Appendix.

items.title: 22.7 Further information
items.text: For details of the Calendar display, visitor controls, event popups, date handling and privacy restrictions, see chapter 19 Calendar in this guide.

items.title: 23 Program design and development notes
items.text:
☑ For creators ☐ For visitors

This part of the Guide records some of the design decisions and implementation details behind Dynamic Web Extended. It is intended mainly for anyone maintaining or extending DWE in the future.

DWE began as a modification of the Gramps Dynamic Web Report (DWR). Wherever practical, the existing DWR structure and behaviour have been retained. Changes have generally been made to add a feature, improve the presentation of existing information, or deal with a particular limitation encountered while using DWR.

Some decisions described here are not obvious from the program code itself. They are recorded so that a future change does not inadvertently undo behaviour that was deliberately chosen.

items.title: 23.1 Relationship data: record rather than infer
items.text:
DWE tries to report genealogical relationships that are explicitly recorded in Gramps rather than infer additional relationships from the surrounding family structure.

This is particularly important for step relationships. A person should be described as a stepchild when that relationship has been recorded in Gramps. DWE does not assume that a child becomes the stepchild of somebody merely because a birth parent subsequently forms another family.

The same principle is used when identifying siblings. DWE can find possible siblings by following the parent-child relationships recorded in Gramps, including non-birth relationships. It then uses shared birth parents to classify full and half-siblings. If a sibling connection is found but no common birth parent is found, DWE describes the person as a non-birth brother, non-birth sister or non-birth sibling, rather than guessing that the relationship is a step-sibling relationship.

This distinction is deliberate. Family structure alone is not sufficient evidence for DWE to create a genealogical relationship that the researcher has not recorded.

items.title: 23.2 Parent-child relationship None
items.text:
An explicit Gramps parent-child relationship of None should not be used for relationship traversal. It indicates that the parent-child relationship does not exist or is considered not to exist, and therefore should not be used to discover parents, siblings or other relatives.

Whether an explicitly recorded None relationship should nevertheless be displayed to a website visitor is a separate presentation question. This remains an area for possible future work.

items.title: 23.3 Multiple families and siblings
items.text:
DWR already supports people belonging to multiple families. DWE makes some changes to the presentation of these families to make less usual family structures easier to follow.

The Parents & siblings display associates children with the appropriate parent family and can also show other families of a person's parents. The inherited option controlling this behaviour is labelled Include children from other families of the parents in DWE and is selected by default.

This option controls presentation only. It does not alter the genealogy used by other DWE features. For example, clearing the option may hide an additional parent family from Parents & siblings, while Tracking can still identify a half-sibling and Events can still include that sibling's events.

The DWR person-family JavaScript coding was corrected so that parent-family information is matched by the actual family index rather than its position in an intermediate list. This is important when a person has several parent families.

DWE also corrects display problems encountered with families containing children but no recorded parents, and with collapse/expand controls in multiple-family displays. Gramps permits a family containing siblings without requiring an artificial unknown father or mother, and DWE can display such a family correctly.

items.title: 23.4 Parent-child relationship wording
items.text:
DWE can alter the wording of standard Gramps parent-child relationship types, and a Parent-child relationship note can override relationship wording. The relationship naming supports the inverse, for example ‘Birth’ could be changed to ‘born to’.

DWE does not maintain a table of default relationship phrases. If no Parent-child relationship note is selected, or if a relationship has no matching entry, the relationship name supplied by Gramps is used.

The note is parsed into a dictionary keyed by the Gramps relationship name. The lookup uses the localized relationship name returned by Gramps, allowing entries to be written in the language used to generate the report. Multiple languages can coexist in the same note, and entry order is not significant.

The optional A and P values allow the kinship word to be placed after or before the relationship phrase. This avoids assuming that English word order is suitable for every language.

The user-supplied relationship phrases are not translated by DWE. The website creator is responsible for providing the standard relationship name and the desired wording.

items.title: 23.5 Translation and Local Labels
items.text:
New interface text intended for translation follows the translation mechanism already used by Gramps. DWE-specific strings are added to the translated-label data where they are required by the generated JavaScript.

Local Labels is a separate mechanism. It allows the report creator to replace translated labels without modifying DWE. Replacement occurs after the normal label has been translated, so the label on the left of a Local Labels definition must correspond to the label in the language being used for the report.

A Local Labels replacement is global to that translated label; it is not associated with one particular page or control. For this reason, a developer should not reuse the same translated string for unrelated purposes merely because the English wording happens to be identical.

items.title: 23.6 Topola Tree Viewer
items.text:
The Tree Viewer is based on Topola Viewer. DWE uses a locally bundled build rather than depending on the online Topola service. The built application is stored under vendor/topola-viewer/dist.

Bundling Topola keeps the generated website self-contained, does not send the family GEDCOM to an external viewer, and avoids cross-site and CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) issues that can arise when the DWE website and the viewer are hosted at different locations. The Tree Viewer and its supporting files are served from the same website as the rest of the DWE report.

DWE generates the GEDCOM only when Include Tree Viewer is selected. The GEDCOM is generated using the Gramps GEDCOM writer and is then sanitised for use by Topola. DWE removes the generated submitter reference, submitter record and generated copyright header so that researcher details are not unnecessarily included in the Tree Viewer data.

DWE's bundled Topola build has also been customised. Among the changes are integration with the DWE person pages, person highlighting, and renaming the export filenames.

Changes to Topola source code are made in the separate Topola source/build directory and rebuilt before the resulting dist files are copied into DWE. Consequently, a future upgrade of Topola must preserve or reapply the DWE modifications rather than simply replacing the bundled files with a new upstream build.

items.title: 23.7 Tree Viewer limitation
items.text: Tree Viewer may fail to render large trees. It appears that Topola is in the process of developing expandable tree controls. This is a path for further investigation. If the Viewer could initially display a limited number of generations and expand the tree on demand, it might avoid the need to render a very large tree at once.

items.title: 23.8 Lifespans and Vega
items.text:
The Lifespans display uses Vega rather than the normal DWR charting code.

DWR generally exports small individual categories of information into separate JavaScript data structures and combines them in the browser. The Lifespans implementation takes a somewhat different approach: much of the information needed to construct a person's timeline row is assembled together for the chart. This was a deliberate implementation choice because the timeline needs several related values at the same time.

Lifespans is person-oriented rather than family-oriented. The chart gathers the subject's parents, siblings, spouses and children and arranges them into those groups. People are de-duplicated where necessary.

Vega export is configured to use lifespans as the download filename and a white chart background, so exported SVG and PNG files have predictable filenames and appearance.

items.title: 23.9 Markdown processing
items.text:
DWE supports three ways of identifying Markdown: the fixed first-line MD marker, a selected Markdown note type, and the Treat ordinary notes as Markdown option.

MD is deliberately a fixed marker rather than a configurable string, making marked notes portable between DWE installations and family trees.

Html code and To Do notes always take precedence over the Markdown mechanisms and are excluded from Markdown processing.

DWE preserves Gramps styled-note formatting and then allows Markdown processing of the resulting content. This permits useful combinations such as a Markdown table within an otherwise normally styled Gramps note. Because Gramps styling and Markdown are two independent formatting systems, unusual combinations may still need to be checked in the generated website.

items.title: 23.10 Gramps styled-note compatibility
items.text:
Gramps 5.2.3's HTML backend does not provide mappings for the Strikethrough and Subscript StyledText types. As a result, the original DWR can fail when it encounters notes containing those styles.

DWE uses its own small extension of the Gramps HTML backend to provide HTML mappings for these styles (\<s> and \<sub>). This retains compatibility with Gramps 5.2 while allowing the normal Gramps implementation to handle the other StyledText types.

items.title: 23.11 Participation events labels
items.text: Participation event labels are two-line labels displayed like this: Marriage followed by (:Best man) for a person with a ‘Best man’ role. The colon identifies participation roles, in case parentheses may be part of an event type name, such as Marriage (Christian).

items.title: 23.12 Diagnostic logging
items.text:
DWE uses the Gramps/Python logging system for development diagnostics.

Normal diagnostic messages should use DEBUG level so that they do not interfere with ordinary Gramps operation. WARNING and particularly ERROR should be reserved for conditions that the user needs to know about; Gramps may present ERROR messages through its error-reporting interface.

Logging output appears in the console when Gramps is started from the console.

items.title: 23.13 Development and source control
items.text:
DWE is maintained as a Git repository. Development changes should normally be made in a separate branch, tested by generating and viewing a report, and committed in small, logical checkpoints.

Generated websites should be tested through a local HTTP server rather than solely with file:// URLs. Some browser features, including the Tree Viewer, require normal web-server behaviour. DWE provides View report locally.bat for convenient local viewing on Windows.

Changes involving bundled third-party components such as Topola should distinguish between changes to the upstream source and the built files stored in the DWE repository.

items.title: 23.14 Browser storage
items.text:
Some DWE display preferences are saved in the browser so that they can be remembered as the visitor moves between pages or returns to the website later.

Web browsers provide two similar forms of storage that can be used for this purpose:

Session storage retains information for the current page session. It can carry a setting between pages while that session continues but is not intended to persist as a long-term preference.

Local storage persists beyond the current browser session. It allows a website to remember a preference when the visitor closes the website and returns to it later.

DWE uses browser storage for some visitor display preferences rather than storing them in the generated family-history data. These settings therefore belong to the browser being used, not to the Gramps family tree or the DWE report options.

Browser storage must be permitted for these preferences to be remembered. Most browsers allow it by default. Private or incognito browsing, clearing site data, or privacy settings that remove or prevent site storage may cause preferences to be lost.

These browser-stored preferences should not be confused with the report options used when generating DWE. Report options are saved in a file by Gramps for the family tree; browser preferences are choices made while viewing the generated website.

items.title: 23.15 Additional CSS and JavaScript
items.text:
DWE retains the CSS and JavaScript structure of the original Dynamic Web Report and adds or modifies files to support its additional features.

The dwr_start.js file loads the JavaScript and style sheets used by the generated website. In addition to the standard DWR files, DWE loads dwr_styles_B.css, which contains additional DWE styling, and timeline-vega.js, which contains JavaScript used for the Lifespans display.

Much of the DWE website behaviour is implemented in the existing DWR JavaScript structure rather than in separate files for every DWE feature. For example, DWE additions to person pages and other displays are integrated with the existing dwr.js processing.

Keeping the additional Lifespans code in timeline-vega.js helps separate the Vega-based graphical display from the larger dwr.js file. Additional DWE CSS in dwr_styles_B.css similarly allows DWE-specific presentation changes to be kept separate from the main DWR style sheet.

items.title: 23.16 Generated website data files
items.text:
DWE reuses the architecture of the original Dynamic Web Report in which much of the genealogical information used by the website is exported into JavaScript data files. The browser uses this data to construct person, family and other displays dynamically rather than requiring a separately generated HTML page containing all the information for each person.

DynamicWebExtended.py exports the principal Gramps objects into JavaScript data structures. These include individuals, families, places, sources, citations, repositories and media. References between objects are generally stored as indexes into the corresponding data structures; for example, an event can contain a place index and citation indexes rather than repeating the complete place and citation records.

DWE extends some of the data inherited from DWR to support its additional features. Person data, for example, includes information used for Lifespan, Why Me, Tracking and Story, as well as the existing person and event information.

Tree Viewer is somewhat different. When Include Tree Viewer is selected, DWE also generates a GEDCOM file for the bundled Topola viewer. This is separate from the JavaScript data used by the normal DWE pages. Before the GEDCOM is included in the generated website, DWE removes the Gramps researcher/submitter information and the automatically generated copyright statement.

The generated website therefore contains both the program files that provide the browser interface and generated data representing the selected family tree. These files belong together: when a generated DWE website is copied to another location or uploaded to a web server, the complete generated directory should be copied.

The generated data filenames reflect these object types. I represents individuals (persons), F families, P places, S sources, C citations, M media and R repositories. The data is divided further into files containing particular fields. For example, dwr_db_I_birth_date_0.js contains extracted birth-date data for individuals. If the data for a field is sufficiently large, it is split across a series of numbered files, such as ..._0.js, ..._1.js, ..._2.js and so on.

items.title: 23.17 Themes
items.text: The original DWR uses the bootstrap system to create its website pages. DWE includes a range of Bootstrap themes from Bootswatch that the creator can choose from to generate the site. A site visitor also has access to the same range of themes, so the visitor can easily override the theme and hence the look of their website by choosing another from the Configuration page.

items.title: 23.18 Notable records — records library
items.text:
The Notable records feature is based on the Gramps librecords.py library, which provides the calculations used to identify individuals and families holding various genealogical records.

DWE currently uses a modified local copy of this library, named dwe_records.py, rather than importing the standard Gramps library directly.

The local version incorporates two improvements:

  • Person with most marriages: Adds a new record category identifying individuals with the greatest number of marriages.

  • Alphabetical sorting: Sorts individuals and families alphabetically when multiple records have the same ranking, providing a consistent and predictable display order.

Both improvements have been submitted to the Gramps project as pull requests:

  • PR #2567 — Person with most marriages

  • PR #2570 — Sort tied Notable Records alphabetically

The intention is to use the standard Gramps librecords.py again once these improvements have been incorporated into Gramps and are available in the supported versions.

The original import statement has been retained as a comment in DynamicWebExtended.py to make this future change easier.

DWE also uses a database adapter to restrict record calculations to the individuals and families included in the generated website, ensuring that the report's privacy and living-person settings are respected.

items.title: 23.19 Calendar birthday names
items.text:
The rules for determining the surname displayed for married women in Calendar birth events are described in the Calendar Options section.

DWE has retained the surname-selection rules from the original Gramps Web Calendar report. The apparent intention is to allow women to be identified by either their own surname or a surname acquired through marriage.

However, determining an appropriate surname is not straightforward, particularly when a woman has multiple marriages or several recorded names. The inherited implementation represents a compromise, using the woman's recorded names and the order of her families in Gramps. The resulting surname may not necessarily be the one she used at the time of a particular event.

items.title: 23.20 Known issues and future work
items.text:
Areas identified for possible future work include:

  • None relationships - deciding whether explicitly recorded None parent-child relationships should optionally be displayed, while continuing to exclude them from relationship traversal;

  • Help page in DWE report options dialog - reviewing the DWE help-page destination rather than retaining the original DWR help link. The help page link is hard coded inside Python – the existing report points it to the original Dynamic Web report help page. I would need to adapt that at some time and point this to its own page;

  • Hyperlink display- reviewing the visual treatment of hyperlinks where themes do not make clickable text sufficiently obvious;

  • Version testing - testing DWE against future Gramps versions in an isolated environment before declaring them supported;

  • Local server window - automatically closing of the local server command window after a user closes the DWE browser page;

  • Optimise media file copying - improving the copy_file() function to avoid unnecessary copying of unchanged files. Currently, DWE (and DWR) copies each source file to a temporary destination and then compares its contents with the existing file, even when the files are identical. Consider using file size, modification timestamps or other methods to identify unchanged files before copying, while ensuring that modified files are reliably detected. This could significantly reduce report generation time for websites containing large numbers of media files, particularly when regenerating an existing website.

items.title: 24 Report generation progress and timing
items.text:
☑ For creators ☐ For visitors

When you click OK to generate a report, Dynamic Web Extended (DWE) displays a progress dialog showing the stages of report generation and the overall percentage completed.

DWE also measures the elapsed time for each stage. These timings are written to the console and can be viewed if Gramps was started from a command-line console. The timing information is primarily intended for technical diagnosis and performance analysis.

items.title: 24.1 Understanding the progress indicator
items.text:
The amount of processing required varies considerably between family trees. For example, a tree containing many media files may spend substantial time copying images and generating thumbnails, while another tree may contain thousands of sources or citations.

The progress indicator does not analyse those differences; it just uses fixed estimates for the different stages. Consequently, the progress bar may advance quickly during some stages and more slowly during others. The percentage displayed is only an estimate of the work completed.

During particularly long operations, Windows may display a message indicating that "Gramps is not responding". This can occur when Gramps is busy processing data and is temporarily unable to respond to Windows. The message will often disappear when processing continues. It does not necessarily indicate that Gramps has stopped working.

items.title: 24.2 Example timing output
items.text:
The following example shows the timing information produced during the generation of a website:

  • DWE TIMING: Building object dictionaries...: 4.583 seconds

  • DWE TIMING: Sorting object dictionaries...: 0.052 seconds

  • DWE TIMING: Preparing website files...: 0.141 seconds

  • DWE TIMING: Exporting individuals...: 15.080 seconds

  • DWE TIMING: Exporting families...: 0.373 seconds

  • DWE TIMING: Exporting sources...: 8.333 seconds

  • DWE TIMING: Exporting citations...: 0.365 seconds

  • DWE TIMING: Exporting repositories...: 0.006 seconds

  • DWE TIMING: Exporting places...: 0.330 seconds

  • DWE TIMING: Exporting media...: 16.462 seconds

  • DWE TIMING: Building surname index...: 0.157 seconds

  • DWE TIMING: Generating HTML pages...: 1.402 seconds

  • DWE TIMING: Generating GENDEX index...: 0.035 seconds

  • DWE TIMING: Generating GEDCOM for Tree Viewer...: 3.725 seconds

  • DWE TIMING: Preparing local viewing files...: 0.003 seconds

  • DWE TIMING: Creating website archive...: 37.773 seconds

  • DWE PROGRESS: 100/100 units completed

  • DWE TIMING: TOTAL report generation: 89.289 seconds

In this example, exporting individuals, media and sources accounted for much of the processing time, though building an archive at the end took the most time. Some stages, such as website archiving, are optional. If not enabled, the timing is still shown.

The actual timings depend on the size and contents of the family tree, the report options selected, and the performance of the computer and its storage devices.

items.title: 25 Appendix
items.text: ☑ For creators ☐ For visitors

items.title: 25.1 Example Gramps notes
items.text:
The following examples provide starting points for some of the special notes that can be used with DWE. They can be copied as they are into Gramps notes and adapted for a particular website.

All these notes are optional. The relevant sections of this guide describe how each note is selected and used.

  • Some example notes such as Events, Lifespans and Tree Viewer are for display directly on the website and use Markdown for convenient formatting. They could alternatively use plain text, or html.

  • The Parent-child relationship and Local labels notes are plain text notes used inside DWE: DWE reads the content and processes it, so they should follow the syntax shown in their examples and should not be formatted as Markdown.

items.title: 25.2 Example Events About note
items.text:
This example note uses DWE's MD marker to render the note contents as Markdown. The MD line will not be displayed on the website.

MD
## 25.3 Events {#events}
The events list has been extended, and brings together events for the person and their family.
You can choose to display:

- the person's own events
- events for their parents
- events for their siblings
- events for their spouses
- events for their children
- events in which the person has a role (called Participation events)

Events are normally shown in date order.  Events without dates cannot be positioned chronologically and are not included when the display is limited to the person's lifespan.

Use the checkboxes above the table to choose the information you want to see.  Your display choices are remembered as you move between people in the website.

Event notes can also be shown or hidden.  Hiding notes can provide a more compact view when many events are displayed.

items.title: 25.4 Example Lifespans About note
items.text:
This example note uses DWE's MD marker to render the note contents as Markdown. The MD line is not displayed on the website.

MD
## 25.5 Lifespans {#lifespans}

This chart shows the lifespans of the person and their immediate family, grouped as parents, siblings, spouses and children.  Marriages are shown as vertical markers.

Select a person's name to open their page in this website.

Use **Date hints** to show or hide date markers, and **Marriages** to show or hide marriage events.  The **Label height** control changes the size of the labels.

The three-dot menu at the top right of the chart can be used to save the chart as an SVG or PNG image.

items.title: 25.6 Example Tree Viewer About note
items.text:
This example note uses DWE's MD marker to render the note contents as Markdown. The MD line is not displayed on the website.

MD
## 25.7 Tree Viewer {#tree-viewer}

The Tree Viewer provides an interactive view of the family tree centred on the current person.

You can pan and zoom the tree, search for another person, and select people to see more information about them.

You can maximise the tree to use the whole browser space.

Select **Open page for this person** to open the selected person's page in this website.

The View options allow different tree layouts to be selected.  The Download options can save the displayed tree as PDF, PNG or SVG.

items.title: 25.8 Example Citations About note
items.text:
This example note uses DWE's MD marker to render the note contents as Markdown. The MD line is not displayed on the website.

MD
### 25.8.1 Citations {#citations}

This section lists the citations associated with the individual. Citations are collected from references throughout the Individual's page, including names, events, family members, relationships, places, media and other items.

Consequently, a citation may appear here even when it is not attached directly to the individual.

When displayed as a table:

- **Citation** identifies the citation, including its Gramps ID when enabled.
- **Source** identifies the source associated with the citation.
- **Cited in** describes where the citation is used. Clicking the description takes you back to the corresponding citation reference on the Individual page.
- **Details** displays the citation's recorded information.

The table can be sorted by column and searched across all columns or within a selected column.

The original list view is available.  You can choose between the two formats on the Configuration page.

items.title: 25.9 Example Parent-child relationship note
items.text:
DWE already contains definitions for the standard Gramps parent-child relationships, so there is no need to copy all the defaults into this note. Include only the relationships whose wording you want to change.

This is not a Markdown note. DWE reads new relationship definitions directly from the note.

See Parent-child relationship note in section 21.6 for the complete syntax and the built-in defaults.

Alternative parent-child relationship phrases
Lines without a > separator can be used as comments.

Adopted > adopting > adopted > A > can produce ‘adopting father’ and ‘adopted son’
Foster > foster > foster > A

items.title: 25.10 Example Local labels note
items.text:
This example shows how to restore the original DWR wording for Ancestors and Descendants, plus a new label for Why Me.

The Local Labels note is not a Markdown note. DWE reads each label replacement directly from the note. See the Local Labels section [21.7](21-dwe-options.md#local-labels-note) for the complete syntax.

Local label changes

Parents & siblings > Ancestors
Spouses & children > Descendants
Why me > Why is this person in the tree?

items.title: 25.11 Example Calendar note
items.text:
This example note uses DWE's MD marker to render the note contents as Markdown. The MD line is not displayed on the website. This shows a note suitable for the Calendar About section.

MD
This calendar shows birth, marriage and death events recorded in the family history, arranged by month and day.

**Selecting events**

Use **Living people only** or **All people** to control which events are displayed.  The events available in the calendar depend on the options selected by the website creator.

**Viewing events**

Dates containing events display a number indicating how many events occurred on that month and day.

- Hover over a date to see a temporary preview of its events.
- Click a date to open a popup that remains visible, allowing you to select a person and visit their Individual page.
- Events are listed with the most recent year first.

**Dates without a known day**

Events with a known month but an unknown day are grouped under an asterisk (*) in the bottom-right cell of that month.

**Leap-day events**

29 February is included in every calendar, so events recorded on that date are always accessible.

The arrangement of weekdays reflects the current year, not the historical weekday on which an event occurred.

**Today button**

Select **Today** to scroll to the current date.
